_how: Recipe for shorts.build (video-machine). 13 clips from Justin Gamblin's (Hendricks Septic Tank Service Inc., Madisonville, Kentucky) guest episode, take 160057 (Zoom HD 1280x720, speaker view, no upscale). Source is the lip-synced file (zoom-160057-synced.mov, Justin 55 ms earlier) with its words file; keep = inclusive word-index ranges in play order; fillers skip automatically; stammers stay in the audio and are hidden from the captions with "" fixes, max_gap 1.0. Justin's phone picture is a portrait window in the middle of the frame, so layout crop at 0.5 frames him exactly. Posting plan: release week 2026-12-09..12-15, every clip to YouTube + TikTok at noon or 5 PM CT; the five strongest (go-empty, walk-right-over, call-100, neighbor-deal, wish-i-hadnt) also to Instagram and Facebook at noon on weekdays. cover_with: with Justin Gamblin of Hendricks Septic Tank Service

clips.title:
Go *empty* to the farthest
septic job first

youtube.title: Why septic trucks should drive empty to the farthest job first

captions.facebook:
Ask a septic pumper what the job really is and Justin Gamblin of {hendricks} in Madisonville, Kentucky will tell you it is trucking. He pumps septic tanks and grease traps, but the money is in the logistics. He tells his guys all the time to run empty to the farthest job and work their way back toward the dump location, because a truck that is loaded at the far end gets worse fuel mileage on the way home. With fuel around $6 a gallon, that kind of planning adds up.

#septic

clips.title:
I walk right over to
the *septic tank*

youtube.title: Septic trade secret: how to find a tank by reading the yard

captions.facebook:
His guys get frustrated with him, and Justin Gamblin of {hendricks} understands why. They will say they cannot find the septic tank, then he walks out in the yard, goes right to it, and they ask how he did that. He says he honestly does not know. The man he bought the business from showed him an easier way to find tanks early on, and he says once you find one you can pretty much find them all. He would rather read the yard than flush a transmitter.

#septic

clips.title:
Call *100* past septic
customers, 10 to 15 book

youtube.title: Septic reminder calls: call 100 customers and 10 to 15 book on the spot

captions.facebook:
The septic business is a roller coaster, and Justin Gamblin of {hendricks} has felt every dip. One thing that helps: a few years ago his team converted their customer history into QuickBooks. When they pump a tank, they ask if the customer wants a reminder and write it on the invoice, and it goes in the computer. Then they call the list. He says if you call 100 people, 10 to 15 of them will book right then.

#septic

clips.title:
Door hangers flopped,
the *neighbor deal* didn't

youtube.title: Septic neighbor discounts: door hangers flopped, the deal still works

captions.facebook:
Justin Gamblin of {hendricks} listened to this podcast, heard about the neighbor discount, and gave it a real try. He kept door hangers in the truck and hung one on the house next door after a job. He says they did not see much turnout from that. But when a customer brings up the neighbor deal, he honors it, and he says you would be surprised how often that works.

#septic

clips.title:
Do I wish I hadn't
bought my *septic* company?

youtube.title: Should you buy a septic company? A Kentucky owner on what he would tell you

captions.facebook:
Does Justin Gamblin of {hendricks} regret buying his septic company? Yes and no. He bought it in 2012 from the man who started it, and some days he says he wishes he had not. But it gave him a head start: an established name, an existing customer list, and grease traps that were already on the books. He does not think buying is a necessity. He says you could start with a truck and a day job and grow from there.

#septic
